genel.secureBootNotu: If you're installing Windows 11, don't touch this setting — leave it on. Only if you're installing Windows 10 and your USB drive doesn't appear in the list at all, try setting the option marked Secure Boot to Disabled.

adimlar.baslik: Plug in the USB drive and shut the computer down
adimlar.aciklama: Plug the USB drive into the computer. Then shut the computer down completely. Not "Sleep" or "Hibernate" — it has to really turn off. Wait until the screen goes fully dark.

adimlar.baslik: Turn it on and start pressing DELETE or F2 right away
adimlar.aciklama: Press the power button. The moment the screen lights up, start pressing DELETE or F2 about once a second and keep pressing. You need to be pressing while the your computer's brand logo is on screen. If Windows starts, you were too late: shut down and try again.

adimlar.baslik: Recognise the settings screen you land on
adimlar.aciklama: A settings screen opens, coloured or grey, in English. This is called the BIOS. The mouse may not work; you move with the arrow keys and choose with Enter. You can't break anything by accident here, because you can leave without saving.

adimlar.baslik: Go to Boot and move the USB to the top
adimlar.aciklama: Use the arrow keys to reach Boot. You'll see an ordered list: the computer picks what to start from by reading this order. Move your USB drive's name (it shows the brand) to the top of this list. Moving is usually done with the + and - keys or F5 / F6; the bottom of the screen says which.

adimlar.baslik: Save with F10 and exit
adimlar.aciklama: Press F10. It asks "Save changes?"; choose Yes and press Enter. The computer restarts and this time starts from the USB drive. If you see the Windows setup screen, everything worked.
